title.zh: 卷一百八十五上 列傳第一百三十五上: 良吏上
title.raw: 卷一百八十五上 列傳第一百三十五上: 良吏上 Volume 185 Biographies 135: Virtuous Officials 1

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝曰：「使政平訟息，民無愁嘆，與我共理，其惟良二千石乎！

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han said: "If government is equitable and lawsuits cease, and the people have no sighs of grief—who shares in governing with me but good prefects at the two-thousand-dan rank!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han said, "When the administration is fair and litigation dies down, when the people are free of sorrow and lament—who governs with me if not worthy prefects at two thousand dan?!"

sentences.zh: 」故漢代命官，重外輕內，郎官出宰百里，郡守入作三公。

translations.literal: Therefore in the Han dynasty's appointment of officials, outer posts were valued and inner posts lightly regarded: gentlemen-attendants went out to govern hundred-li districts, and prefects came in to become the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the Han appointed officials, they prized service in the provinces over posts at court: palace gentlemen went out to rule districts, and prefects were brought in to serve as the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 世祖中興，尤深吏術，慎選名儒為輔相，不以吏事責功臣；

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty, he was especially thorough in the art of administration, carefully selecting renowned Confucians as chief ministers and not holding meritorious officials accountable for routine administrative duties;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu revived the Han, he took official administration especially seriously, choosing distinguished scholars as chief ministers and not burdening meritorious generals with routine bureaucratic work;

sentences.zh: 政優則增秩賜金，績負則論輸左校。

translations.literal: if governance was excellent they received rank increases and gifts of gold; if performance was deficient they were sentenced to penal service at the Left Construction Corps.
translations.idiomatic: those who governed well were promoted and given gold; those whose records fell short were sentenced to labor at the Left Construction Corps.

sentences.zh: 選任之道，皇漢其優。

translations.literal: In the way of selection and appointment, the Grand Han excelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the matter of choosing and appointing officials, the Han stood supreme.

sentences.zh: 隋政不綱，彜倫斯紊。

translations.literal: Sui government lacked guiding principles, and moral order was thrown into disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Sui rule lost its bearings, and the moral order collapsed.

sentences.zh: 天子事巡遊而務征伐，具僚逞側媚而竊恩權。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven busied himself with tours of inspection and pursued military campaigns, while the full complement of officials flaunted servile flattery and usurped favor and power.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor occupied himself with imperial tours and campaigns of conquest, while his entire staff practiced obsequious flattery and stole favor and authority for themselves.

sentences.zh: 是時朝廷無正人，方嶽無廉吏。

translations.literal: At that time the court had no upright men, and the regional governors had no incorrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: In those days the court held no upright men, and the provinces had no honest magistrates.

sentences.zh: 跨州連郡，莫非豺虎之流；

translations.literal: Across provinces and linking commanderies, none were other than wolf-and-tiger types;
translations.idiomatic: Spanning provinces and linking commanderies, every officeholder was a wolf or tiger in human form;

sentences.zh: 佩紫懷黃，悉奮爪牙之毒。

translations.literal: wearing purple and clutching yellow seals, all wielded the venom of claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: bedecked in purple and clutching yellow seals, they all bared the poison of fang and claw.

sentences.zh: 以至土崩不救，旋踵而亡。

translations.literal: So that the realm collapsed beyond rescue and perished in the turning of a heel.
translations.idiomatic: Until the empire disintegrated beyond saving and fell in the blink of an eye.

sentences.zh: 武德之初，余風未殄。

translations.literal: In the early Wude era, surviving habits had not yet been extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: In the first years of Wude, the old corrupt ways had not yet died out.

sentences.zh: 太宗皇帝削平亂跡，湔洗汙風，唯思稼穡之艱，不以珠璣為寶。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong leveled the traces of disorder and washed away corrupt customs, thinking only of the hardship of tilling and sowing and not regarding pearls and gems as treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong swept away the wreckage of rebellion and cleansed a tainted age, mindful only of how hard the farmers toiled and never treating pearls and jade as his treasure.

sentences.zh: 以是人知恥格，俗尚貞修，太平之基，率由茲道。

translations.literal: Therefore people knew shame and restraint, custom honored integrity and self-cultivation, and the foundation of great peace derived largely from this path.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the people learned shame and self-restraint, custom prized integrity, and the foundations of lasting peace were laid largely along this road.

sentences.zh: 洎天後、玄宗之代，貞元、長慶之間，或以卿士大夫涖方州，或以御史、郎官宰畿甸，行古道也，所病不能。

translations.literal: Down through the eras of Empress Wu and Emperor Xuanzong and the intervals of Zhenyuan and Changqing, sometimes grand masters and court gentlemen oversaw regional prefectures, sometimes censors and gentlemen-attendants governed the capital districts—the ancient way was practiced, but the flaw was that it could not be sustained.
translations.idiomatic: By the reigns of Empress Wu and Emperor Xuanzong, and in the Zhenyuan and Changqing periods, grandees or censors and palace gentlemen might govern provinces or the capital region—the old ideal was still pursued, but the trouble was that it could not be kept up.

sentences.zh: 自武德已還，歷年三百，其間嶽牧，不乏循良。

translations.literal: From Wude onward, spanning three hundred years, among the regional governors there was no lack of upright and benevolent men.
translations.idiomatic: From Wude down through three hundred years, the ranks of provincial governors never lacked men who were upright and kind in office.

sentences.zh: 今錄其政術有聞，為之立傳，所冀表吏師而儆不恪也。

translations.literal: Now we record those whose administrative methods were renowned and compose biographies for them, hoping to display models for officials and warn those who are not diligent.
translations.idiomatic: We now record those whose governance won renown and write their biographies, hoping to hold up teachers for officials and warn the negligent.

sentences.zh: 韋仁壽，雍州萬年人也。

translations.literal: Wei Renshou was a native of Wannian in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Renshou came from Wannian in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為蜀郡司法書佐，斷獄平恕，其得罪者皆曰：「韋君所斷，死而無恨。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign he served as judicial clerk in Shu Commandery; he judged cases with fairness and clemency, and those he condemned all said, "In what Lord Wei decided, one could die without resentment."
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daye era he served as judicial clerk in Shu Commandery, deciding cases with fairness and mercy; even those he condemned said, "In Lord Wei's judgment one could die without regret."

sentences.zh: 」高祖入關，遣使定巴蜀，使者承制拜仁壽巂州都督府長史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered the Pass, he sent envoys to secure Bashu; an envoy, acting on imperial order, appointed Renshou long secretary of the Suizhou Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered the Pass he sent envoys to pacify Bashu; an envoy acting on imperial authority appointed Renshou long secretary of the Suizhou Directorate.

sentences.zh: 時南寧州內附，朝廷每遣使安撫，類皆受賄，邊人患之，或有叛者。

translations.literal: At that time Nanning Prefecture had submitted; the court often sent envoys to reassure the region, and they almost all accepted bribes, to the distress of the border people, and some rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Nanning had recently submitted to the court, but the envoys sent to pacify the region almost always took bribes; the frontier people suffered, and some rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 高祖以仁壽素有能名，令檢校南寧州都督，寄聽政於越巂，使每歲一至其地以慰撫之。

translations.literal: Because Renshou had long been known for ability, Gaozu ordered him to act as inspector of the Nanning Prefecture commandant, with his seat of government at Yuexi, and to come once each year to that region to comfort and reassure it.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, knowing Renshou's reputation for competence, made him acting commandant of Nanning while basing his administration at Yuexi, with orders to visit the region once a year to reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 仁壽將兵五百人至西洱河，承制置八州十七縣，授其豪帥為牧宰，法令清肅，人懷歡悅。

translations.literal: Renshou led five hundred troops to the Western Er River, and by imperial commission established eight prefectures and seventeen counties, appointing local chieftains as governors; the laws were clear and strict, and the people were filled with joy.
translations.idiomatic: Renshou marched five hundred men to the Western Er River and, by imperial authority, set up eight prefectures and seventeen counties, installing local chiefs as magistrates; his rule was orderly and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 及將還，酋長號泣曰：「天子遣公鎮撫南寧，何得便去？

translations.literal: When he was about to return, the chieftains wailed and said, "The Son of Heaven sent you, sir, to pacify Nanning—how can you leave so soon?"
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to leave, the chiefs wept aloud: "The Son of Heaven sent you to govern Nanning—how can you go away so soon?"

sentences.zh: 」仁壽以城池未立為辭，諸酋長乃相與築城，立廨舍，旬日而就。

translations.literal: Renshou pleaded that the city walls had not yet been built; the chieftains then joined together to build a city and erect official quarters, completing the work in ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Renshou replied that no walled city had yet been built; the chiefs then joined forces to raise walls and government buildings, finishing in ten days.

sentences.zh: 仁壽又曰：「吾奉詔但令巡撫，不敢擅住。

translations.literal: Renshou said again, "I received orders only to tour and reassure; I dare not stay on my own authority."
translations.idiomatic: Renshou said again, "My commission is only to inspect and reassure—I dare not remain without authorization."

sentences.zh: 」及將歸，蠻夷父老各揮涕相送。

translations.literal: When he was about to go home, the tribal elders of the barbarians all waved tears as they saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: When he set out for home, the tribal elders came out weeping to bid him farewell.

sentences.zh: 因遣子弟隨之入朝，貢方物，高祖大悅。

translations.literal: They then sent their sons and younger kinsmen to follow him to court with tribute of local products, and Gaozu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: They sent their sons to accompany him to court with local tribute, and Gaozu was delighted.

sentences.zh: 仁壽復請徙居南寧，以兵鎮守。

translations.literal: Renshou again requested to move his residence to Nanning and garrison it with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Renshou again asked to move his seat to Nanning and hold it with troops.

sentences.zh: 有詔特聽以便宜從事，令益州給兵送之。

translations.literal: An edict specially permitted him to act as circumstances required, and ordered Yizhou to supply troops to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict specially authorized him to act at discretion, and ordered Yizhou to provide troops to escort him there.

sentences.zh: 刺史竇軌害其功，托以蜀中山獠反叛，未遑遠略，不時發遣。

translations.literal: The prefect Dou Gui, jealous of his achievement, pleaded that the mountain Liao in Shu had rebelled and that distant campaigns could not be undertaken, and did not send the troops in time.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Dou Gui, resentful of his success, claimed that the mountain tribes of Shu had rebelled and that distant operations could not be attempted, and failed to dispatch the troops on schedule.

sentences.zh: 經歲餘，仁壽病卒。

translations.literal: After more than a year, Renshou died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Renshou died of illness.

sentences.zh: 朕以隋末亂離，毒被海內；

translations.literal: I consider that at the end of the Sui, turmoil and separation spread, and calamity covered the realm within the seas;
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that at the end of the Sui, chaos and separation afflicted the entire empire;

sentences.zh: 率土百姓，零落殆盡，州裏蕭條，十不存一；

translations.literal: the people throughout the land were scattered and nearly gone, prefectures and districts were desolate, and not one in ten remained;
translations.idiomatic: the people across the land were scattered and all but gone, the provinces lay waste, and scarcely one in ten survived;

sentences.zh: 寤寐思之，心焉若疚。

translations.literal: waking and sleeping I think of it, and my heart is as if afflicted with guilt.
translations.idiomatic: I think of it waking and sleeping, and my heart is heavy with guilt.

sentences.zh: 是以日昃忘食，未明求衣，曉夜孜孜，惟以安養為慮。

translations.literal: Therefore I forget to eat when the sun slants, seek my robes before dawn, and toil day and night, thinking only of securing and nurturing the people.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I forget my meal when the sun is low, rise before dawn, and labor day and night with no thought but how to shelter and nourish my people.

sentences.zh: 每見水旱降災，霜雹失所，撫躬責己，自慚德薄。

translations.literal: Whenever I see flood or drought bring disaster, or frost and hail fall out of season, I lay hand on myself and blame my person, ashamed that my virtue is thin.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever flood or drought strikes, or frost and hail come out of season, I blame myself and feel ashamed that my virtue is insufficient.

sentences.zh: 恐貧乏之黎庶，不免饑餒；

translations.literal: I fear that the impoverished common people cannot escape hunger and cold;
translations.idiomatic: I fear that the poor among my people cannot escape hunger;

sentences.zh: 傾竭倉廩，普加賑恤。

translations.literal: I empty the granaries and extend relief everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: I have emptied the granaries and extended relief throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 其有一人絕食，若朕奪之，分命庶僚，盡心匡救。

translations.literal: If even one person goes without food, it is as if I had taken it from him; I charge all my officials to devote their hearts to aiding and saving them.
translations.idiomatic: If even one person goes hungry, it is as though I had stolen his food; I charge every official to do his utmost to save them.

sentences.zh: 去年關內六州及蒲、虞、陜、鼎等復遭亢旱，禾稼不登，糧儲既少，遂令分房就食。

translations.literal: Last year the six prefectures within the Pass and Pu, Yu, Shan, Ding, and the like again suffered severe drought; the grain crops did not mature, stores were already low, and I therefore ordered households to disperse to find food.
translations.idiomatic: Last year the six prefectures of Guanzhong and Pu, Yu, Shan, Ding, and the like suffered drought again; the harvest failed and stores ran low, so I ordered families to move elsewhere for food.

sentences.zh: 比聞刺史以下及百姓等並識朕懷，逐糧戶到，遞相安養，回還之日，各有贏糧。

translations.literal: I have lately heard that prefects and below and the common people alike understood my intent: following the grain-seeking households, they received and cared for one another in turn, and on the day of return each had surplus grain.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that prefects and the people alike understood my purpose: they followed the grain-seeking households, sheltered one another in turn, and when they returned each family brought surplus grain home.

sentences.zh: 乃別賫布帛，以申贈遺，如此用意，嘉嘆良深。

translations.literal: They even brought cloth and silk separately as gifts in parting; such intent moves me to deep praise and sighing.
translations.idiomatic: They even brought cloth and silk as parting gifts; such thoughtfulness fills me with deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 一則知水旱無常，彼此遞相拯贍，不慮兇年。

translations.literal: First, I know that flood and drought are unpredictable, yet people rescue and support one another in turn and do not fear famine years.
translations.idiomatic: First, I see that though flood and drought are unpredictable, people now rescue one another in turn and no longer dread famine.

sentences.zh: 二則知禮讓興行，輕財重義，四海士庶，皆為兄弟。

translations.literal: Second, I know that courtesy and yielding flourish, that people value righteousness over wealth, and that gentlemen and commoners throughout the four seas are all as brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Second, I see courtesy and yielding on the rise, people prizing duty over wealth, and men everywhere treating one another as brothers.

sentences.zh: 變澆薄之風，敦仁慈之俗，政化如此，朕復何憂。

translations.literal: The shallow and mean wind is transformed, and the custom of kindness and benevolence is made thick; when government and transformation are thus, what further worry have I?
translations.idiomatic: The shallow ways of the past are changing and a kinder custom is taking root; with governance like this, what have I left to fear?

sentences.zh: 其安置客口，官人支配得所，並令考司錄為功最。

translations.literal: Those who settled the guest households and assigned officials appropriately are all to have the evaluation office record this as their highest achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Those officials who settled the migrant households wisely are to have this recorded as their finest achievement in the evaluation records.

sentences.zh: 養戶百姓，不吝財帛，已敕主者免今年調物。

translations.literal: The common people who sheltered households did not spare cloth and silk; I have already ordered the responsible offices to exempt this year's tax levies.
translations.idiomatic: The people who took in others did not spare their goods; I have ordered that this year's tax levies be waived for them.

sentences.zh: 宜知此意，善相勸勉。

translations.literal: You should understand this intent and encourage one another well.
translations.idiomatic: Let everyone understand my meaning and encourage one another accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其年，入為太府少卿，轉少府少監。

translations.literal: That year he entered the capital as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then was transferred to vice superintendent of the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was summoned to the capital as vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, then promoted to vice superintendent of the Palace Workshops.

sentences.zh: 九年，坐事除名。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was struck from the rolls for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was dismissed from office for an offense.

sentences.zh: 後起授虔州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was reappointed and made prefect of Qianzhou, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reappointed prefect of Qianzhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 張允濟，青州北海人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Yunji was a native of Beihai in Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yunji came from Beihai in Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中為武陽令，務以德教訓下，百姓懷之。

translations.literal: During the Daye era of Sui he was magistrate of Wuyang, devoting himself to instructing the people through virtue, and the common people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era he served as magistrate of Wuyang, governing through moral instruction, and the people loved him.

sentences.zh: 元武縣與其鄰接，有人以牸牛依其妻家者八九年，牛孳產至十余頭；

translations.literal: Yuanwu County bordered his district; a man had left a cow with his wife's family for eight or nine years, and the herd had increased to more than ten head;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanwu County bordered his district; a man had left a cow with his wife's family for eight or nine years, and the herd had grown to more than ten head;

sentences.zh: 及將異居，妻家不與，縣司累政不能決。

translations.literal: when he was about to live separately the wife's family would not return them, and the county office through successive administrations could not decide the case.
translations.idiomatic: when he was about to set up a separate household the wife's family refused to return the cattle, and the county magistrates over several terms could not settle the dispute.

sentences.zh: 其人詣武陽質於允濟。

translations.literal: The man went to Wuyang to lay the case before Yunji.
translations.idiomatic: The man went to Wuyang to seek judgment from Yunji.

sentences.zh: 允濟曰：「爾自有令，何至此也？

translations.literal: Yunji said, "You have your own magistrate—why come here?"
translations.idiomatic: Yunji said, "You have your own magistrate—why bring this to me?"

sentences.zh: 」其人垂泣不止，具言所以。

translations.literal: The man wept without cease and told the whole story.
translations.idiomatic: The man wept without stopping and told him the whole story.

sentences.zh: 允濟遂令左右縛牛主，以衫蒙其頭，將詣妻家村中，雲捕盜牛賊，召村中牛悉集，各問所從來處。

translations.literal: Yunji then had his attendants bind the owner of the cattle, cover his head with a shirt, and take him to the wife's village, saying they were capturing a cattle thief; he summoned all the cattle in the village and asked each where it came from.
translations.idiomatic: Yunji had his men bind the cattle owner, hood him with a shirt, and lead him to the wife's village claiming they had caught a cattle thief; he gathered every cow in the village and asked who owned each one.

sentences.zh: 妻家不知其故，恐被連及，指其所訴牛曰：「此是女婿家牛也，非我所知。

translations.literal: The wife's family did not know the reason and, fearing implication, pointed to the cattle in dispute and said, "These are the son-in-law's cattle, not mine to know about."
translations.idiomatic: The wife's family, not knowing the ruse and fearing implication, pointed to the disputed cattle and said, "Those belong to our son-in-law—I know nothing about them."

sentences.zh: 」允濟遂發蒙，謂妻家人曰：「此即女婿，可以牛歸之。

translations.literal: Yunji then removed the hood and said to the wife's family, "This is the son-in-law—you may return the cattle to him."
translations.idiomatic: Yunji removed the hood and told the wife's family, "Here is your son-in-law—give him back his cattle."

sentences.zh: 」妻家叩頭服罪。

translations.literal: The wife's family kowtowed and acknowledged their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The wife's family kowtowed and confessed their wrong.

sentences.zh: 元武縣司聞之，皆大慚。

translations.literal: When the officials of Yuanwu County heard of it, they were all deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: When the magistrates of Yuanwu heard of it, they were deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 又嘗道逢一老母種蔥者，結庵守之。

translations.literal: He also once met on the road an old woman growing scallions who had built a hut to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road he met an old woman growing scallions who had built a hut to guard her crop.

sentences.zh: 允濟謂母曰：「但歸，不煩守也。

translations.literal: Yunji said to her, "Just go home—there is no need to stand guard."
translations.idiomatic: Yunji told her, "Go home—there is no need to keep watch."

sentences.zh: 若遇盜，當來告令。

translations.literal: If thieves come, you should report to the magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: If thieves come, report to me.

sentences.zh: 」老母如其言，居一宿而蔥大失。

translations.literal: The old woman did as he said; after one night most of the scallions were lost.
translations.idiomatic: The old woman did as he said; after one night most of her scallions were stolen.

sentences.zh: 母以告允濟。

translations.literal: The old woman reported it to Yunji.
translations.idiomatic: She reported the theft to Yunji.

sentences.zh: 悉召蔥地十里中男女畢集，允濟呼前驗問，果得盜蔥者。

translations.literal: He summoned all the men and women within ten li of the scallion field, called them forward and questioned them, and indeed found the scallion thief.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned every man and woman within ten li of the field, questioned them, and found the thief.

sentences.zh: 曾有行人候曉先發，遺衫於路，行十數里方覺。

translations.literal: Once a traveler waiting for dawn set out early and left his shirt on the road, walking more than ten li before he noticed.
translations.idiomatic: Once a traveler waiting for dawn set out early, left his shirt on the road, and walked more than ten li before he noticed.

sentences.zh: 或謂曰：「我武陽境內，路不拾遺，但能回取，物必當在。

translations.literal: Someone said to him, "Within Wuyang under my rule, no one picks up what others lose on the road—if you only go back, the thing will surely still be there."
translations.idiomatic: Someone told him, "In Wuyang under Magistrate Zhang, no one picks up lost property—go back and you will find your shirt still there."

sentences.zh: 」如言果得。

translations.literal: As he was told, he indeed found it.
translations.idiomatic: He went back and found it just as predicted.

sentences.zh: 遠近稱之。

translations.literal: Near and far praised him.
translations.idiomatic: People near and far praised him.

sentences.zh: 政績尤異。

translations.literal: His administrative achievements were especially outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: His record in office was especially distinguished.

sentences.zh: 遷高陽郡丞，時無郡將，允濟獨統大郡，吏人畏悅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be assistant prefect of Gaoyang; at the time there was no commandery governor, and Yunji alone governed the great commandery; clerks and people both feared and rejoiced in him.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant prefect of Gaoyang; with no commandery governor in place, Yunji alone governed the large commandery, and officials and people alike respected and loved him.

sentences.zh: 及賊帥王須拔攻圍，時城中糧盡，吏人取槐葉槁節食之，竟無叛者。

translations.literal: When the bandit chief Wang Xuba attacked and besieged the city, grain in the city was exhausted and clerks and people ate locust-tree leaves and withered stalks, yet in the end none rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Wang Xuba besieged the city and food ran out, officials and people ate locust leaves and dried stalks, yet not one turned traitor.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，累遷刑部侍郎，封武城縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of justice and enfeoffed as Baron of Wucheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he rose to vice minister of justice and was enfeoffed as Baron of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 出為幽州刺史，尋卒。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Youzhou and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Youzhou and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 李桐客，冀州衡水人也。

translations.literal: Li Tongke was a native of Hengshui in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tongke came from Hengshui in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為門下錄事。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as a recorder in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as a recorder in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大業末，煬帝幸江都，時四方兵起，謀欲徙都丹陽，召百僚會議。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, Emperor Yang favored Jiangdu; at that time armies rose in the four directions, and the court planned to move the capital to Danyang and summoned the hundred officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daye, Emperor Yang was at Jiangdu; rebellion spread everywhere, and the court planned to move the capital to Danyang and summoned the officials to debate the move.

sentences.zh: 公卿希旨，俱言「江右黔黎，皆思望幸，巡狩吳會，勒石紀功，復禹之跡，今其時也。

translations.literal: The high ministers curried favor and all said, "The common people south of the Yangtze all long to behold the imperial presence; a tour of inspection to Wu and Kuaiji, inscribing stone to record merit and renewing the traces of Yu—now is the time."
translations.idiomatic: The high ministers echoed the emperor's wish and declared, "The people south of the Yangtze yearn for the Son of Heaven; a tour to Wu and Kuaiji, carving stone to commemorate his deeds and retracing Yu's path—now is the moment."

sentences.zh: 」桐客獨議曰：「江南卑濕，地狹州小，內奉萬乘，外給三軍，吳人力屈，不堪命。

translations.literal: Tongke alone argued, "The south of the Yangtze is low and damp, the land narrow and the prefectures small; within it must support the imperial carriage, and without supply the three armies—the people of Wu are exhausted in strength and cannot bear the burden."
translations.idiomatic: Tongke alone objected: "The Jiangnan region is low and damp, its territory narrow and its prefectures small; it must support the imperial court within and supply the armies without—the people of Wu are exhausted and cannot bear the strain."

sentences.zh: 且逾越險阻，非社稷之福。

translations.literal: Moreover, to cross over steep barriers is not a blessing to the altars of soil and grain."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, crossing such dangerous terrain would bring no blessing to the state."

sentences.zh: 」御史奏桐客謗毀朝政，僅而獲免。

translations.literal: The censor memorialized that Tongke had slandered court policy, and he barely escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: A censor accused Tongke of slandering the government, and he barely escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 後隋滅，從宇文化及至黎陽，轉沒竇建德。

translations.literal: After the Sui fell he followed Yuwen Huaji to Liyang, then fell into the hands of Dou Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: After the Sui fell he followed Yuwen Huaji to Liyang, then was captured by Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 建德平，太宗召授秦府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Jiande was defeated, Taizong summoned him and appointed him legal adjutant of the Prince of Qin's mansion.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande was defeated, Taizong summoned him and made him legal adjutant in the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，累遷通、巴二州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted through Tong and Ba prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he served successively in Tong and Ba prefectures.

sentences.zh: 所在清平流譽，百姓呼為慈父。

translations.literal: Wherever he was, his governance was clear and tranquil and his reputation spread; the common people called him the kindly father.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served his rule was fair and his fame spread; the people called him the kindly father.

sentences.zh: 後卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at home.

sentences.zh: 李素立，趙州高邑人，北齊梁州刺史義深曾孫也。

translations.literal: Li Suli was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Prefecture, a great-grandson of Yi Shen, prefect of Liangzhou under Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Suli came from Gaoyi in Zhao Prefecture and was a great-grandson of Yi Shen, who had been prefect of Liang under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 祖駼，散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tu was attendant at the palace library.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tu served as attendant at the palace library.

sentences.zh: 父政藻，隋水部郎中，大業末充使淮南，為盜所殺。

translations.literal: His father Zhengzao was a director in the Ministry of Waterways under Sui; at the end of Daye he was sent on a mission to Huainan and was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhengzao was a director in the Ministry of Waterways; late in Daye he was sent on a mission to Huainan and was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 素立，武德初為監察御史。

translations.literal: Suli, at the beginning of Wude, was a surveillance censor.
translations.idiomatic: Suli became a surveillance censor early in the Wude era.

sentences.zh: 時有犯法不至死者，高祖特命殺之，素立諫曰：「三尺之法，與天下共之，法一動搖，則人無所措手足。

translations.literal: At the time someone had violated the law but not to the point of death; Gaozu specially ordered him executed. Suli remonstrated, "The law measured in three feet is shared with all under Heaven; if the law is shaken once, people have nowhere to set hand or foot."
translations.idiomatic: When a man had broken the law but not in a capital offense, Gaozu ordered him executed anyway. Suli remonstrated: "The law belongs to all under Heaven; if it is bent once, no one will know where he stands."

sentences.zh: 陛下甫創鴻業，遐荒尚阻，奈何輦轂之下，便棄刑書？

translations.literal: Your Majesty has only just founded great enterprise, and distant wilds are still obstructed—how, beneath the imperial carriage-hub, can you cast aside the penal code?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has only just founded the dynasty and distant regions are still unsettled—how can you abandon the penal code here at the capital?"

sentences.zh: 臣忝法司，不敢奉旨。

translations.literal: I, unworthy, hold office in the law bureau and dare not obey the order."
translations.idiomatic: I serve in the law office and dare not carry out such an order."

sentences.zh: 」高祖從之。

translations.literal: Gaozu followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 自是屢承恩顧。

translations.literal: From then on he repeatedly received imperial favor and attention.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he enjoyed repeated imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 素立尋丁憂，高祖令所司奪情，授以七品清要官，所司擬雍州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter Suli entered mourning for a parent; Gaozu ordered the relevant offices to have him set aside mourning feelings and appointed him to a seventh-rank position that was both prestigious and substantial; the offices proposed him as administrative assistant for household registration in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Suli entered mourning, Gaozu had him recalled from mourning and appointed to a seventh-rank post of distinction and responsibility; the officials proposed making him aide for household registration in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「此官要而不清。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "This office is substantial but not prestigious."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "That post is important but lacks prestige."

sentences.zh: 」又擬秘書郎。

translations.literal: " Again they proposed him as secretary of the palace library.
translations.idiomatic: They then proposed making him secretary in the palace library.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「此官清而不要。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "This office is prestigious but not substantial."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "That one is prestigious but not important."

sentences.zh: 」遂擢授侍御史，高祖曰：「此官清而復要。」

translations.literal: " Thereupon he was promoted and appointed attendant censor; Gaozu said: "This office is both prestigious and substantial.""
translations.idiomatic: So he was promoted to attendant censor. Gaozu said: "This post is both prestigious and important."

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累轉揚州大都督府司馬。

translations.literal: During the Zhenguan era he was repeatedly transferred until he became deputy secretary of the Yangzhou supreme area command.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he rose through several posts to become deputy secretary at the Yangzhou area command.

sentences.zh: 時突厥鐵勒部相率內附，太宗於其地置瀚海都護府以統之，以素立為瀚海都護。

translations.literal: At that time the Tiele tribes of the Turks successively submitted and came within the borders; Taizong established the Hanhai Area-Protection Office in their territory to oversee them, and appointed Suli as Hanhai area protector.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiele tribes of the Turks submitted one after another, Taizong created the Hanhai protectorate to govern them and made Suli its protector.

sentences.zh: 又有闕泥孰別部，猶為邊患。

translations.literal: There was also the Que-ni-shu separate division, which still constituted a border trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The Que-ni-shu branch remained a border threat.

sentences.zh: 素立遣使招諭降之。

translations.literal: Suli sent envoys to summon and instruct them, and they surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Suli sent envoys to win them over, and they submitted.

sentences.zh: 夷人感其惠，率馬牛以饋素立，素立唯受其酒一杯，余悉還之。

translations.literal: The barbarians were moved by his kindness and brought horses and cattle as gifts to Suli; Suli accepted only one cup of wine and returned all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were grateful for his goodwill and brought horses and cattle as gifts; Suli accepted only a single cup of wine and returned everything else.

sentences.zh: 為建立廨舍，開置屯田。

translations.literal: For them he built official quarters and opened military-agricultural colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He built government offices for them and established military farm settlements.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉綿州刺史。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to be prefect of Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he became prefect of Mian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，遷蒲州刺史，及將之任，所余糧儲及什物，皆令州司收之，唯賫己之書籍而去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui he was moved to be prefect of Puzhou; when he was about to take up his appointment, the remaining grain stores and goods he left behind he had the prefectural offices collect; he took only his own books and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yonghui he was appointed prefect of Pu Prefecture; when he left for his new post he turned over all surplus grain and supplies to the prefecture and took away only his personal books.

sentences.zh: 道病卒，高宗聞而特為廢朝一日，謚曰平。

translations.literal: He died of illness on the road; when Gaozong heard of it he specially suspended court for one day and gave him the posthumous name Ping.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died en route; on hearing of it Gaozong canceled court for a day and posthumously named him Ping.

sentences.zh: 其孫至遠，有重名。

translations.literal: His grandson Zhiyuan had a weighty reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhiyuan enjoyed wide renown.

sentences.zh: 長壽中為天官郎中。

translations.literal: During the Changshou era he served as a director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changshou period he served as a director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 內史李昭德重其才，薦於則天，擢令知流內選事。

translations.literal: Chief minister Li Zhaode valued his talent, recommended him to Empress Wu, and promoted him to oversee the inner-stream selection of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Li Zhaode recognized his ability, recommended him to Empress Wu, and had him put in charge of inner-court official selection.

sentences.zh: 或勸至遠謝其私恩，至遠曰：「李公以公見用，豈得以私謁也。

translations.literal: Some urged Zhiyuan to go thank him for the private favor; Zhiyuan said: "Lord Li recommended me on grounds of the public good—how could one make a private visit of thanks?"
translations.idiomatic: Some advised Zhiyuan to pay a personal visit of thanks; he replied: "Lord Li recommended me on merit—how could I visit him as a private favor?"

sentences.zh: 」竟不謝，遂為昭德所銜，因事出為壁州刺史卒。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not thank him; consequently Zhaode nursed a grievance, and on some pretext had him sent out to be prefect of Bizhou, where he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to do so, earning Zhaode's resentment; Zhaode eventually had him transferred to be prefect of Bi Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 至遠子畬，初為汜水主簿。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan's son She, at first was recorder of Sishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan's son She began as recorder of Sishui County.

sentences.zh: 處事敏速，有聲稱，雖村童廁養之輩，一閱之後，無不知替代姓名者。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he was quick and sharp and had a reputation for it; even village children and latrine attendants, once he had looked at them once, there were none who did not know the names of those scheduled for rotation.
translations.idiomatic: He handled business with remarkable speed and earned a strong reputation; even village boys and latrine workers—once he had reviewed their records, he knew every man scheduled for rotation by name.

sentences.zh: 累轉國子司業。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred until he became vice president of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to vice president of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 事母甚謹，閨門邕睦，累代同居。

translations.literal: In serving his mother he was extremely careful; within the inner gates harmony prevailed, and generations lived together.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply devoted to his mother; his household was harmonious, with many generations living together.

sentences.zh: 每歲時拜慶，長幼男女，咸有禮節。

translations.literal: Whenever seasonal congratulatory visits were made, elders and youths, men and women, all had proper ritual decorum.
translations.idiomatic: On every seasonal family gathering, young and old alike observed the proper ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 及妻卒，時母已先病，畬恐傷母意，約家人不令哭聲使聞於母，朝夕定省，不曾見其憂念之色，士友甚以此稱之。

translations.literal: When his wife died, his mother was already ill; She feared hurting his mother's feelings, so he made an agreement with the family not to let sounds of weeping reach his mother; morning and evening he attended upon her, and she never once saw a look of worry or distress on his face; scholars and friends greatly praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife died his mother was already ill; fearing to grieve her, She had the family keep mourning cries from her ears and visited her morning and evening without ever showing distress; his peers greatly admired him for this.

sentences.zh: 及母終，過毀，卒於喪。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was excessive in damaging his health through mourning and died during the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned so excessively that he died during the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 至遠弟從遠，景雲中歷黃門侍郎、太府卿。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan's younger brother Congyuan, during the Jingyun era successively held the posts of vice minister of the Secretariat and minister of the Court of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan's younger brother Congyuan served as vice minister of the Secretariat and minister of the Imperial Treasury during the Jingyun period.

sentences.zh: 素立從兄子遊道，則天時官至冬官尚書、同鳳閣鸞臺三品。

translations.literal: Suli's older male cousin's son Youdao, during the time of Empress Wu reached the posts of minister of the Ministry of Works and third-rank associate of the Phoenix Pavilion and Luan Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Suli's cousin's son Youdao rose under Empress Wu to minister of works and third-rank associate of the executive secretariat.

sentences.zh: 薛大鼎，蒲州汾陽人，周太子少傅博平公善孫也。

translations.literal: Xue Dading was a native of Fenyang in Puzhou, a grandson of the Duke of Boping, Shan, former junior tutor to the crown prince under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Dading came from Fenyang in Pu Prefecture and was a grandson of Duke Boping Shan, who had been tutor to the Zhou crown prince.

sentences.zh: 父粹，隋介州長史。

translations.literal: His father Cui was chief secretary of Jie Prefecture under Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cui had been chief secretary of Jie Prefecture under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒謀反，授絳州刺史，諒敗伏誅。

translations.literal: When Prince Han Liang plotted rebellion, he was appointed prefect of Jiang Prefecture; when Liang was defeated he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han Liang rebelled, Cui was appointed prefect of Jiang Prefecture; after Liang's defeat he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 大鼎以年幼免死，配流辰州，後得還鄉里。

translations.literal: Dading, because he was young, was spared death and sentenced to penal transportation to Chen Prefecture; later he was able to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Dading escaped execution because of his youth and was exiled to Chen Prefecture; he was eventually allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 義旗初建，於龍門謁高祖，因說：「請勿攻河東，從龍門直渡，據永豐倉，傳檄遠近，則足食足兵。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was first raised, he called on Gaozu at Longmen and urged: "Please do not attack Hedong; cross directly from Longmen, seize Yongfeng Granary, and dispatch proclamations far and near—then you will have ample food and ample troops."
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion began he visited Gaozu at Longmen and advised him not to attack Hedong but to cross the river there, seize Yongfeng Granary, and proclaim his cause throughout the region to secure both provisions and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 既總天府，據百二之所，斯亦拊背扼喉之計。

translations.literal: Once you control the granary of Heaven, holding the place of the one-over-a-hundred strategic chokepoint, this is likewise the plan of patting the back and gripping the throat."
translations.idiomatic: Once you hold the imperial storehouse and the strategic gateway to the realm, you will have your enemy by the throat."

sentences.zh: 」高祖深然之。

translations.literal: " Gaozu deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was strongly convinced.

sentences.zh: 時將士鹹請先攻河東，遂從眾議。

translations.literal: At the time officers and soldiers all requested attacking Hedong first, so he followed the assembled opinion.
translations.idiomatic: The troops all wanted to attack Hedong first, and he yielded to them.

sentences.zh: 授大將軍府察非掾。

translations.literal: Dading was appointed investigating clerk of the grand general's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigative clerk on the staff of the grand general.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累轉鴻臚少卿、滄州刺史。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was repeatedly transferred until he became vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and prefect of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he became vice minister of state ceremonial and prefect of Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州界有無棣河，隋末填廢。

translations.literal: Within the prefecture's borders was the Wudi River, which at the end of Sui had been filled in and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Wudi River within his jurisdiction had been filled in and abandoned at the end of the Sui.

sentences.zh: 大鼎奏開之，引魚鹽於海。

translations.literal: Dading memorialized to open it and brought fish and salt by connecting it to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Dading had it reopened, linking it to the sea for fish and salt.

sentences.zh: 百姓歌之曰：「新河得通舟楫利，直達滄海魚鹽至。

translations.literal: The common people sang of it: "The new river now allows boats to pass with profit; straight through to the blue sea, fish and salt arrive."
translations.idiomatic: The people sang: "The new canal carries boats with ease; fish and salt now come straight from the sea."

sentences.zh: 昔日徒行今騁駟，美哉薛公德滂被。

translations.literal: Formerly one walked on foot—now one drives four-horse teams; how beautiful is Lord Xue's virtue, spreading like a great flood!"
translations.idiomatic: Where we once walked on foot we now ride in carriages—how magnificent is Lord Xue's generous virtue!"

sentences.zh: 」大鼎又以州界卑下，遂決長蘆及漳、衡等三河，分泄夏潦，境內無復水害。

translations.literal: " Dading also, because the prefecture's territory was low-lying, opened the Changlu and Zhang, Heng, and other three rivers to divide and discharge the summer floods; within the borders there were no more water disasters.
translations.idiomatic: Dading also diverted the Changlu, Zhang, and Heng rivers to drain summer floods from the low-lying prefecture, ending flooding in the region.

sentences.zh: 時與瀛州刺史賈敦頤、曹州刺史鄭德本，俱有美政，河北稱為「鐺腳刺史」。

translations.literal: At the time together with Jia Dunyi, prefect of Yingzhou, and Zheng Deben, prefect of Caozhou, all had excellent governance; Hebei called them the "tripod-legged prefects."
translations.idiomatic: He, Jia Dunyi of Ying Prefecture, and Zheng Deben of Cao Prefecture were all renowned administrators; people in Hebei called them the "tripod-legged prefects."

sentences.zh: 永徽四年，授銀青光祿大夫，行荊州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yonghui he was granted the silver-green glory-emolument grandee and acted as chief secretary of the Jingzhou supreme area command.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 4 he was made a silver-green grandee of merit and acting chief secretary at the Jingzhou area command.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 有二子：克構、克勤。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Kegou and Keqin.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons, Kegou and Keqin.

sentences.zh: 克構，天授中官至麟臺監。

translations.literal: Kegou, during Tian shou reached the office of director of the Directorate of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tian shou period Kegou became director of the imperial library.

sentences.zh: 克勤，歷司農少卿，為來俊臣所陷伏誅。

translations.literal: Keqin successively served as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries; he was framed by Lai Junchen and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Keqin served as vice minister of the imperial granaries but was framed by Lai Junchen and executed.

sentences.zh: 克構坐配流嶺表而死。

translations.literal: Kegou by association was sentenced to penal transportation beyond the Ling Mountains and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Kegou was implicated and exiled to the far south, where he died.

sentences.zh: 賈敦頤，曹州冤句人也。

translations.literal: Jia Dunyi was a native of Yuanqu in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Dunyi came from Yuanqu in Cao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，歷遷滄州刺史。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he was transferred through several posts until he became prefect of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan he was appointed prefect of Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 在職清潔，每入朝，盡室而行，唯弊車一乘，羸馬數匹；

translations.literal: In office he was pure and clean; whenever he went to court the whole household went with him—only one worn-out carriage and a few emaciated horses;
translations.idiomatic: He served with strict integrity; whenever he traveled to court his entire household rode in a single battered carriage drawn by a few skinny horses;

sentences.zh: 羈勒有闕，以繩為之，見者不知其刺史也。

translations.literal: where bridles and reins were lacking, rope was used in their place; those who saw this did not know he was a prefect.
translations.idiomatic: with rope substituting for broken bridles—observers had no idea he was a prefect.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，轉瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to be prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he became prefect of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州界滹沱河及滱水，每歲泛溢，漂流居人，敦頤奏立堤堰，自是無復水患。

translations.literal: Within the prefecture's borders were the Hutuo River and the Xu River; each year they overflowed and swept away residents; Dunyi memorialized to build dikes and dams, and from then on there were no more water disasters.
translations.idiomatic: The Hutuo and Xu rivers flooded annually, carrying away homes; Dunyi built dikes and ended the flooding.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，累遷洛州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was repeatedly promoted until he became prefect of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 5 he was appointed prefect of Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時豪富之室，皆籍外占田；

translations.literal: At the time the houses of the powerful and wealthy all kept registers of lands held outside their allotments;
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families then kept lands beyond their registered allotments;

sentences.zh: 敦頤都括獲三千余頃，以給貧乏。

translations.literal: Dunyi in a comprehensive tally recovered more than three thousand qing and gave them to the poor and destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Dunyi recovered over three thousand qing of such land and distributed it to the poor.

sentences.zh: 又發奸摘伏，有若神明。

translations.literal: He also exposed wrongdoing and extracted confessions, as if he were a divine being.
translations.idiomatic: He also exposed crime with almost supernatural insight.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 弟敦實。

translations.literal: His younger brother Dunshi.
translations.idiomatic: He had a younger brother, Dunshi.

sentences.zh: 敦實，貞觀中為饒陽令，政化清靜，老幼懷之。

translations.literal: Dunshi, during Zhenguan was magistrate of Raoyang; his government and transformation were pure and quiet, and old and young cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan Dunshi served as magistrate of Raoyang with such fair and tranquil governance that young and old alike loved him.

sentences.zh: 時敦頤復授瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Dunyi was again appointed prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Dunyi was reappointed prefect of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊制，大功以上不復連官。

translations.literal: Under the old regulation, for relatives within the degree of major mourning, holding linked offices was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom, close relatives were not allowed to serve in the same jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其兄弟在職，俱有能名，竟不遷替。

translations.literal: The court, because both brothers held office and each had a reputation for ability, in the end did not transfer or replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Because both brothers served capably and enjoyed fine reputations, the court made an exception and left them in their posts.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，累轉洛州長史，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng he was repeatedly transferred until he became chief secretary of Luozhou and had very benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianheng 1 he became chief secretary of Luo Prefecture, governing with notable benevolence.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽令楊德幹杖殺人吏，以立威名，敦實曰：「政在養人，義須存撫，傷生過多，雖能亦不足貴也。

translations.literal: At the time Yang Degan, magistrate of Luoyang, beat officials and clerks to death to establish a fearsome reputation; Dunshi said: "Government lies in nurturing the people; righteousness requires cherishing and soothing them—if lives harmed are too many, even if one has ability it is not worth honoring."
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang magistrate Yang Degan was beating subordinates to death to build a reputation for toughness; Dunshi said: "Government is about nurturing people, not slaughtering them—no matter how capable an official is, wanton killing wins no honor."

sentences.zh: 」常抑止德幹，德幹亦為之稍減。

translations.literal: " He constantly restrained Degan, and Degan for his sake somewhat reduced it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly restrained Yang, who gradually moderated his conduct.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷太子右庶子。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to be right vice tutor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he was appointed right vice tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 初敦頤為洛州刺史，百姓共樹碑於大市通衢；

translations.literal: Earlier when Dunyi was prefect of Luozhou, the common people jointly erected a stele at the main market crossroads;
translations.idiomatic: When Dunyi had been prefect of Luo Prefecture, the people had erected a memorial stele at the main market crossroads;

sentences.zh: 及敦實去職，復刻石頌美，立於兄之碑側，時人號為「棠棣碑」。

translations.literal: when Dunshi left office they again carved stone in praise, setting it beside his elder brother's stele; people of the time called it the "Stele of Tangdi."
translations.idiomatic: when Dunshi left office the people carved another inscription of praise beside his brother's stele, calling it the "Brothers' Stele."

sentences.zh: 敦實後為懷州刺史。

translations.literal: Dunshi later became prefect of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dunshi later served as prefect of Huai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永淳初，以年老致仕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchun, because of old age he retired.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongchun era he retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 及病篤，子孫迎醫視之，敦實曰：「未聞良醫能治老也。

translations.literal: When his illness became grave his sons and grandsons summoned physicians to examine him; Dunshi said: "I have never heard that a good physician can cure old age."
translations.idiomatic: When he fell gravely ill his family sent for doctors; Dunshi said: "I have never heard of a doctor who could cure old age."

sentences.zh: 」終不服藥。

translations.literal: " In the end he never took medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He refused all medicine.

sentences.zh: 垂拱四年卒，時年九十余。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chuigong he died, at the time aged over ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chuigong 4, aged over ninety.

sentences.zh: 子膺福，先天中，歷左散騎常侍、昭文館學士，坐預竇懷貞等謀逆伏誅。

translations.literal: His son Yingfu, during Xiantian successively served as left regular attendant and academician of the Zhaowen Hall; he was executed for participating in the treasonous plot of Dou Huaizhen and others.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yingfu served as left attendant and Zhaowen Hall academician during the Xiantian period but was executed for joining Dou Huaizhen's conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 李君球，齊州平陵人也。

translations.literal: Li Junqiu was a native of Pingling in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Junqiu came from Pingling in Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父義滿，屬隋亂，糾合宗黨，保固村閭，外盜不敢侵逼，以功累授齊郡通守。

translations.literal: His father Yiman, amid the chaos of Sui, rallied clan and kin, fortified and secured the village hamlets, and outer bandits did not dare encroach or press upon them; for merit he was repeatedly appointed until he became surrogate prefect of Qi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui collapse his father Yiman rallied their clan to defend the local community, keeping bandits at bay; for this service he rose to acting prefect of Qi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 武德初，遠申誠款，詔以其宅為譂州，仍拜為總管，封平陵郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he sent a distant declaration of sincere loyalty; an edict made his residence Qian Prefecture and still appointed him area commander, ennobling him as Duke of Pingling Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude he offered his allegiance to the Tang; the court made his estate into Qian Prefecture, appointed him its military governor, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Pingling.

sentences.zh: 君球少任俠，頗涉書籍。

translations.literal: Junqiu in youth was chivalrous and bold and had somewhat penetrated into books and classics.
translations.idiomatic: Junqiu was a man of adventurous spirit in youth and well read.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，齊州都督齊王據州城舉兵作亂，君球與兄子行均守縣城。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan the Prince of Qi, area commander of Qizhou, seized the prefectural city and raised troops in rebellion; Junqiu together with his nephew's son Xingjun guarded the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan the Prince of Qi rebelled and seized the prefectural city; Junqiu and his nephew Xingjun held the county seat.

sentences.zh: 事平，太宗聞而嘉之，擢授遊擊將軍，仍改其本縣為全節縣。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled Taizong heard of it and commended them; he promoted and appointed Junqiu as mobile general and furthermore changed his home county to Quanjie County.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was crushed Taizong praised them, promoting Junqiu to mobile general and renaming his county Quanjie—"Whole Integrity."

sentences.zh: 君球累補左驍衛、義全府折沖都尉。

translations.literal: Junqiu was repeatedly appointed and supplemented until he became area-commandant of the Yiquan Garrison in the Left Brave Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Junqiu eventually became area-commandant of the Yiquan garrison in the Left Brave Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 龍朔三年，高宗將伐高麗，君球上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: In the third year of Longshuo Gaozong was about to attack Goguryeo; Junqiu submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 3, as Gaozong prepared to invade Goguryeo, Junqiu submitted a memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 臣聞心之病者，不能緩聲；

translations.literal: I have heard that one whose heart is ill cannot speak in a gentle voice;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when the heart is stricken one cannot speak softly;

sentences.zh: 事之急者，不能安言；

translations.literal: when affairs are urgent one cannot speak in a calm manner;
translations.idiomatic: when matters are urgent one cannot speak calmly;

sentences.zh: 性之慈者，不能隱情。

translations.literal: one whose nature is compassionate cannot conceal feelings.
translations.idiomatic: and the compassionate cannot hide their true feelings.

sentences.zh: 且食君之祿者，死君之事。

translations.literal: Moreover, one who eats the ruler's salary dies for the ruler's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those who receive the ruler's salary owe their lives to his service.

sentences.zh: 今臣食陛下之祿矣，其敢愛身乎？

translations.literal: Now I eat Your Majesty's salary—how would I dare cherish my own person?
translations.idiomatic: I receive Your Majesty's salary—how could I hold back for fear of my own safety?

sentences.zh: 臣聞《司馬法》曰：「國雖大，好戰必亡；

translations.literal: I have heard that the Methods of Sima says: "Though a state be great, if it loves warfare it must perish;
translations.idiomatic: I have read in the Methods of Sima: "Even a great state will perish if it loves war;

sentences.zh: 天下雖安，忘戰必危。

translations.literal: though all under Heaven be at peace, if one forgets warfare one must face danger."
translations.idiomatic: and even in peace, forgetting war invites disaster."

sentences.zh: 」兵者，兇器，戰者，危事，故聖主明王重行之也。

translations.literal: " Arms are an inauspicious instrument; warfare is a dangerous affair—therefore sage rulers and enlightened kings treat their use with gravity.
translations.idiomatic: Arms are instruments of violence and war a perilous undertaking—sage rulers therefore treat both with the utmost caution.

sentences.zh: 愛人力之盡，恐府庫之殫，懼社稷之危，生中國之患。

translations.literal: I cherish the exhaustion of human strength, fear the depletion of the treasury, dread danger to the altars of state, and the birth of calamity within the Central Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: I fear exhausting the people, draining the treasury, endangering the state, and bringing calamity upon the realm.

sentences.zh: 故古人云：「務廣德者昌，務廣地者亡。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancients said: "One who devotes himself to broadening virtue flourishes; one who devotes himself to broadening territory perishes."
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "Those who cultivate virtue prosper; those who expand territory perish."

sentences.zh: 」昔秦始皇好戰不已，至於失國，是不愛其內而務其外故也。

translations.literal: " In former times Qin Shihuang loved warfare without cease and in the end lost his state—this was because he did not cherish what was within but devoted himself to what was without.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Shihuang's ceaseless love of war cost him his empire because he neglected his own people while chasing conquest abroad.

sentences.zh: 漢武遠討朔方，殆乎萬里，廣拓南海，分為八郡；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han campaigned far to subdue the northern frontier, nearly ten thousand li; he broadly expanded the southern sea and divided it into eight commanderies;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han marched nearly ten thousand li to subdue the northern frontier and pushed south to divide the coast into eight commanderies;

sentences.zh: 終於戶口減半，國用空虛。

translations.literal: in the end household registers were halved and state revenues were empty and depleted.
translations.idiomatic: until half the population was gone and the treasury stood empty.

sentences.zh: 至於末年，方垂哀痛之詔，自悔其失。

translations.literal: Reaching his final years, he only then issued an edict of grief and pain, himself regretting his errors.
translations.idiomatic: Only in his final years did he issue an edict of remorse, acknowledging his mistakes.

sentences.zh: 彼高麗者，辟側小醜，潛藏山海之間，得其人不足以彰聖化；

translations.literal: That Goguryeo—an insignificant petty state lurking hidden between mountains and seas—gaining its people would not be enough to manifest sagely transformation;
translations.idiomatic: As for Goguryeo, it is a petty, insignificant state hiding away between mountains and seas; winning over its people would not be enough to display the power of sage rule;

sentences.zh: 棄其地不足以損天威。

translations.literal: abandoning its territory would not be enough to diminish Heaven's authority.
translations.idiomatic: and abandoning its land would not be enough to diminish the imperial majesty of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 何至乎疲中國之人，傾府庫之實，使男子不得耕耘，女子不得蠶織！

translations.literal: Why go so far as to exhaust the people of China, drain the treasury's reserves, and keep men from plowing and women from raising silkworms and weaving!
translations.idiomatic: Why go so far as to wear out the people of China, drain the treasury dry, and keep men from tilling the fields and women from raising silkworms and weaving!

sentences.zh: 陛下為人父母，不垂惻隱之心，傾其有限之貲，貪於無用之地。

translations.literal: Your Majesty acts as father and mother to the people, yet shows no heart of compassion, spending limited resources in pursuit of useless land.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is father and mother to the people, yet shows no compassionate concern, spending limited resources in greed for useless territory.

sentences.zh: 設令高麗既滅，即不得不發兵鎮守，少發則兵威不足，多發則人心不安，是乃疲於轉戍，萬姓無聊生也。

translations.literal: Supposing Goguryeo were destroyed, troops would have to be sent to garrison it: too few and military authority would be insufficient; too many and the people's hearts would be unsettled—thus worn out by rotating frontier garrison duty, the myriad commoners would have no way to live.
translations.idiomatic: If Goguryeo were destroyed, troops would have to be sent to garrison it: too few and military authority would fall short; too many and the people's hearts would be unsettled. The realm would be worn out by rotating frontier garrison duty, and the myriad commoners would have no way to make a living.

sentences.zh: 萬姓無聊，即天下敗矣！

translations.literal: When the myriad commoners have no way to live, the realm is lost!
translations.idiomatic: When the myriad commoners have no way to live, the realm is lost!

sentences.zh: 天下既敗，陛下何以自安？

translations.literal: Once the realm is lost, how will Your Majesty find peace for yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Once the realm is lost, how will Your Majesty find peace for yourself?

sentences.zh: 故臣以為征之不如不征，滅之不如不滅。

translations.literal: Therefore your subject believes that campaigning is not as good as not campaigning, and destruction is not as good as not destroying.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore your subject believes that campaigning is not as good as not campaigning, and destroying them is not as good as not destroying them.

sentences.zh: 書奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.

sentences.zh: 尋遷蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to the post of prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to serve as prefect of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，改為興州刺史。

translations.literal: Before departing, he was reassigned as prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, he was reassigned as prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: After successive promotions he became chief secretary of the Yangzhou Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: After successive promotions he became chief secretary of the Yangzhou Area Command.

sentences.zh: 政尚嚴肅，人吏憚之，盜賊屏跡，高宗頻降書勞勉。

translations.literal: His governance was marked by severity; officials and clerks feared him, and bandits vanished from sight. Emperor Gaozong repeatedly sent letters of commendation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was stern and austere; officials and clerks feared him, and bandits disappeared entirely. Emperor Gaozong repeatedly sent letters of commendation and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 時有吐谷渾犯塞，以君球素有威重，轉為靈州都督。

translations.literal: At the time Tuyuhun were raiding the border; because Junqiu had long been known for authority and prestige, he was transferred to serve as area commander of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Tuyuhun were raiding the frontier; because Junqiu had long been known for authority and prestige, he was transferred to serve as area commander of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died in office.

sentences.zh: 崔知溫，許州鄢陵人。

translations.literal: Cui Zhiwen was a native of Yanling in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhiwen was a native of Yanling in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖樞，司農卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shu served as Minister of the National Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shu served as Minister of the National Granaries.

sentences.zh: 父義真，陜州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yizhen was prefect of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yizhen was prefect of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 知溫初為左千牛。

translations.literal: Zhiwen initially served as a Left Palace Escort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen initially served as a Left Palace Escort.

sentences.zh: 麟德中，累轉靈州都督府司馬。

translations.literal: During the Linde era, after successive transfers he became vice-governor of the Lingzhou Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: During the Linde era, after successive transfers he became vice-governor of the Lingzhou Area Command.

sentences.zh: 州界有渾、斛薛部落萬余帳，數侵掠居人，百姓鹹廢農業，習騎射以備之。

translations.literal: Within the command's territory were more than ten thousand tents of Hun and Khushe tribes, who repeatedly raided the settled population; the common people all abandoned agriculture and trained in mounted archery to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Within the command's territory were more than ten thousand tents of Hun and Khushe tribes, who repeatedly raided the settled population; the common people all abandoned farming and trained in mounted archery to defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 知溫表請徙於河北，斛薛不願遷移。

translations.literal: Zhiwen submitted a memorial requesting their relocation north of the Yellow River, but the Khushe were unwilling to move.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen submitted a memorial requesting their relocation north of the Yellow River, but the Khushe were unwilling to move.

sentences.zh: 時將軍契苾何力為之言於高宗，遂寢其奏。

translations.literal: At the time the general Qieli Heli spoke on their behalf to Emperor Gaozong, and the memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the general Qieli Heli spoke on their behalf to Emperor Gaozong, and the memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 知溫前後十五上詔，竟從之，於是百姓始就耕獲。

translations.literal: Zhiwen submitted memorials on fifteen separate occasions, and in the end the request was granted; only then did the common people return to plowing and harvesting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen submitted memorials on fifteen separate occasions, and in the end the request was granted; only then did the common people return to plowing and harvesting.

sentences.zh: 後斛薛入朝，因過州謝曰：「前蒙奏徙河北，實有怨心。

translations.literal: Later, when the Khushe came to court and passed through the command, they thanked him, saying: "Previously, when you memorialized to move us north of the Yellow River, we truly harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Khushe came to court and passed through the command, they thanked him, saying, "Previously, when you memorialized to move us north of the Yellow River, we truly harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 然牧地膏腴，水草不乏，部落日富，始荷公恩。

translations.literal: Yet the pasturelands are rich and fertile, water and grass are plentiful, the tribe grows wealthier day by day, and we now owe you a debt of gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the pasturelands are rich and fertile, water and grass are plentiful, the tribe grows wealthier day by day, and we now owe you a debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 」拜伏而去。

translations.literal: " They bowed prostrate and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " They bowed prostrate and departed.

sentences.zh: 知溫四遷蘭州刺史。

translations.literal: After four promotions Zhiwen became prefect of Lanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After four promotions Zhiwen became prefect of Lanzhou.

sentences.zh: 會有党項三萬余眾來寇州城，城內勝兵既少，眾大懼，不知所為。

translations.literal: It happened that more than thirty thousand Tangut troops came to attack the prefectural city; the able-bodied soldiers within the walls were few, and the people were greatly afraid, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that more than thirty thousand Tangut troops came to attack the prefectural city; the able-bodied soldiers within the walls were few, and the people were greatly afraid, not knowing what to do.

sentences.zh: 知溫使開城門延賊，賊恐有伏，不敢進。

translations.literal: Zhiwen had the city gates opened to invite the enemy in, but the enemy feared an ambush and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen had the city gates opened to invite the enemy in, but the enemy feared an ambush and did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 俄而將軍權善才率兵來救，大破党項之眾。

translations.literal: Before long the general Quan Shancai led troops to the rescue and routed the Tangut force.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the general Quan Shancai led troops to the rescue and routed the Tangut force.

sentences.zh: 善才因其降，欲盡坑之，以絕後患，知溫曰：「弗逆克奔，古人之善戰。

translations.literal: Shancai, because they had surrendered, wished to bury them all alive to eliminate future trouble. Zhiwen said: "Not pursuing those who flee is the mark of a good fighter in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Shancai, because they had surrendered, wished to bury them all alive to eliminate future trouble. Zhiwen said, "Not pursuing those who flee is the mark of a good fighter in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 誅無噍類，禍及後昆。

translations.literal: To slaughter every living mouth brings calamity upon later generations.
translations.idiomatic: To slaughter every living soul brings calamity upon later generations.

sentences.zh: 又溪谷崢嶸，草木幽蔚，萬一變生，悔之何及！

translations.literal: Moreover, the ravines and valleys are rugged, and the trees and grass are dense and dark—if trouble should arise, how could one regret it in time!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the ravines and valleys are rugged, and the trees and grass are dense and dark—if trouble should arise, regret would come too late!

sentences.zh: 」善才然其計。

translations.literal: " Shancai approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: " Shancai approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 又欲分降口五百人以與知溫。

translations.literal: He also wished to divide five hundred surrendered captives and give them to Zhiwen.
translations.idiomatic: He also wished to divide five hundred surrendered captives and give them to Zhiwen.

sentences.zh: 知溫曰：「向論安危之策，乃公事也，豈圖私利哉！

translations.literal: Zhiwen said: "When I spoke earlier of strategies for safety and danger, that was public business—how could I seek private gain!
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen said, "When I spoke earlier of strategies for safety and danger, that was public business—how could I seek private gain!

sentences.zh: 」固辭不受。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " He firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 党項余眾由是悉來降附。

translations.literal: Because of this, the remaining Tangut forces all came to surrender and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, the remaining Tangut forces all came to surrender and submit.

sentences.zh: 知溫累遷尚書左丞，轉黃門侍郎、同中書門下三品，兼修國史。

translations.literal: After successive promotions Zhiwen became Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, then transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery with concurrent rank as Third Rank Counselor, and also supervised compilation of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: After successive promotions Zhiwen became Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, then transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery with concurrent rank as Third Rank Counselor, and also supervised compilation of the National History.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年七月，遷中書令。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Yonglong, he was transferred to Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the second year of Yonglong, he was transferred to Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 永淳三年三月卒，年五十七，贈荊州大都督。

translations.literal: He died in the third month of the third year of Yongchun, at the age of fifty-seven, and was posthumously granted the title of Area Commander of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of the third year of Yongchun, at the age of fifty-seven, and was posthumously granted the title of Area Commander of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子泰之，開元中官至工部尚書。

translations.literal: His son Taizhi reached the post of Minister of Works during the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: His son Taizhi reached the post of Minister of Works during the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 少子諤之。

translations.literal: His younger son was Ouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son was Ouzhi.

sentences.zh: 諤之，神龍初為將作少匠，預誅張易之有功，封博陵縣侯，賜實封二百戶。

translations.literal: Ouzhi, in the early Shenlong era served as Vice Director of Palace Construction; for his merit in the execution of Zhang Yizhi he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Boling County and granted two hundred taxable households.
translations.idiomatic: Ouzhi, in the early Shenlong era served as Vice Director of Palace Construction; for his merit in the execution of Zhang Yizhi he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Boling County and granted two hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 開元初，累遷少府監。

translations.literal: In the early Kaiyuan era, after successive promotions he became Superintendent of the Palace Manufactories.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaiyuan era, after successive promotions he became Superintendent of the Palace Manufactories.

sentences.zh: 知溫兄知悌。

translations.literal: Zhiwen's elder brother was Zhi Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwen's elder brother was Zhi Ti.

sentences.zh: 知悌，高宗時官至戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Zhi Ti, during the reign of Emperor Gaozong, reached the post of Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Ti, during the reign of Emperor Gaozong, reached the post of Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 俄起授壽州刺史，政存寬惠，百姓安之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was recalled and appointed prefect of Shouzhou; his governance was lenient and benevolent, and the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was recalled and appointed prefect of Shouzhou; his governance was lenient and benevolent, and the common people were at peace.

sentences.zh: 每行部，必先召學官。

translations.literal: Whenever he made an inspection tour, he always summoned the education officials first.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he made an inspection tour, he always summoned the education officials first.

sentences.zh: 見諸生，試其講誦，訪以經義及時政得失，然後問及墾田獄訟之事。

translations.literal: When he met the students, he tested their lecturing and recitation, inquired about the meaning of the classics and the gains and losses of current policy, and only then asked about land reclamation and lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: When he met the students, he tested their lecturing and recitation, inquired about the meaning of the classics and the gains and losses of current policy, and only then asked about land reclamation and lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 咸亨二年，召拜正諫大夫，兼檢校禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianheng he was summoned and appointed Chief Remonstrance Officer, concurrently serving as acting Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianheng he was summoned and appointed Chief Remonstrance Officer, concurrently serving as acting Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 尋遷黃門侍郎、同中書門下三品，兼修國史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery with concurrent rank as Third Rank Counselor, and also supervised compilation of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery with concurrent rank as Third Rank Counselor, and also supervised compilation of the National History.

sentences.zh: 俄轉御史大夫，累表固辭煩劇之任，高宗嘉其意，拜右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief; he repeatedly submitted memorials firmly declining the onerous post, and Emperor Gaozong commended his intentions and appointed him Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief; he repeatedly submitted memorials firmly declining the onerous post, and Emperor Gaozong commended his intentions and appointed him Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 又請致仕，許之。

translations.literal: He again requested retirement, and the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He again requested retirement, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 永淳二年十月，卒於家，年八十二，贈越州都督府。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Yongchun he died at home, at the age of eighty-two, and was posthumously granted the title of Area Commander of Yuezhou.
